items.title: SAPO reports bail set in alleged Transnistria draft-evasion smuggling case
items.summary: SAPO says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court set bail at 500,000 hryvnias for a suspect investigators consider the organizer of a scheme to smuggle military-age men through Transnistria into Europe. The court also imposed travel and reporting restrictions; investigators have completed the pretrial investigation and opened case materials to the defence.

items.title: Ryabkov says European visit to Moscow would not join Ukraine talks format
items.summary: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Moscow could promptly arrange a visit by representatives of three European countries if they accept its invitation. He stressed that the invitation does not mean European representatives would join the existing Russia-US-Ukraine negotiating format.

items.title: Smolensk governor reports damage to energy site and home after Ukrainian attack
items.summary: Smolensk regional governor Vasily Anokhin said an overnight large-scale Ukrainian attack damaged an energy facility, a civilian industrial site and a private residence in the Russian region. His statement did not specify casualties or the extent of the damage.

items.title: Kyiv water supply disrupted after strikes damage utility infrastructure
items.summary: Local utility services reportedly said Kyivvodokanal facilities were damaged and attacks on the power system disrupted water supplies in the capital. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged residents to work remotely where possible because of damaged bridges, while emergency power cuts were also reported in Dnipropetrovsk region.
